title: formal-learning-theory-kernel, explained
h1: The fundamental theorem of statistical learning in Lean 4: PAC learnability, VC dimension, compression, online and Gold-style learning
lead: For a binary concept class, the Lean proves that finite VC dimension is equivalent to realizable PAC learnability, and also to finite compression with side information (Moran–Yehudayoff), uniformly vanishing Rademacher complexity and Sauer–Shelah growth. It also proves the Littlestone characterization of online learning and Gold's theorem, with no sorry in the library. One catch matters: the PAC results assume that every subset of the domain is measurable, which covers ℕ but not ℝⁿ with its Borel sets.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of Dhruv Gupta's (Zetesis Labs) Lean 4 formal learning theory kernel: the five-way fundamental theorem of statistical learning, Moran–Yehudayoff compression, the Littlestone and Gold characterizations, the paradigm separations, and what the measurability assumptions really cover.
startNote: Start with the headline fundamental_theorem. Its core is vc_characterization (PAC ⟺ finite VC). To read its statement you need PACLearnable, VCDim and MeasurableConceptClass; read the last one closely, because it carries the strongest assumption. The Roadmap lists the whole PAC proof in dependency order. The other paradigms start at littlestone_characterization (online) and gold_theorem (learning in the limit).
sizeNote: About 29,900 lines of Lean in 102 library files (FLT_Proofs/), about 8,000 of them in the newer IndependentVC/ folder; plus about 2,000 lines of verification harness and experimental tactic tests, not covered here.
agentCtx: A Lean 4 + Mathlib library (Dhruv Gupta, Zetesis Labs) formalizing statistical learning theory: the 5-way fundamental theorem (PAC ⟺ finite VC ⟺ compression ⟺ Rademacher ⟺ Sauer–Shelah growth), Littlestone and Gold characterizations, paradigm separations, PAC-Bayes, and measurability theory for symmetrization.
